critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: Make explicit how the closing frames identify the grasped end: V80–V112 show the fingers gripping the beige end of the initially rightmost peg, not its blue end. Map that beige grasp segment back to E0 and approach its demonstrated grasp point, approximately x=-0.0469, y=0.1938, z=0.20 m, yaw=-0.0238. My x=-0.101 targeted the opposite, blue end; matching the peg identity and axis alone did not resolve the grasp location.

The descent rule should distinguish the elevated approach location from the demonstrated contact location instead of requiring the same nominal x,y. Here the pickup contact is about 1.3 cm farther in +x than my chosen approach-aligned target: descend and close at approximately [-0.0469, 0.1938, 0.01], with yaw -0.0238. Use the demonstrated closing grasp offset along the selected peg and current wrist geometry to locate that contact point; being above the peg at z=0.20 does not imply that the approach x,y is the final grasp x,y.

The demonstrated approach geometry needed a more explicit mapping to the TCP: use the completed elevated transport configuration around V160, before descent, to place the TCP near [0.0381, -0.2513, 0.1907], not 4.4 cm farther outward at y=-0.295. Resolve the yaw sign using the held-to-free-end direction in those frames: the free blue end must point into the selected box face, giving yaw approximately -1.3928, not the pi-reversed 1.73. This cycle shows a completed pickup lift, so choose that elevated transport pose with the gripper closed.

The descent rule did not specify how to recover the low staging target precisely from the demonstration rather than rounding the elevated endpoint. At E150, matching V160, the next target is approximately [0.0378, -0.2518, 0.0407]: about 1.1 cm toward -x and 0.9 cm toward +y from the reported TCP as well as downward. Clarify how to fit the demonstrated low pre-advance pose and held-tip alignment to obtain this lateral correction; treating descent as keeping x,y near [0.05, -0.26] misses the recorded target.

At E185, matching demonstration V192, the completed initial advance should be followed by only about 0.023 m further inward, to TCP [0.0229, -0.1827, 0.0401], with the gripper closed and insertion yaw maintained. The instruction to fit the terminal demonstration configuration did not specify how to recover that short remaining displacement from the partly occluded gripper and peg; I instead inferred a roughly 0.060 m advance and overshot. Clarify the box-relative terminal TCP/grasp offset for this configuration rather than treating the visible free-tip or box position as the TCP destination.

The instructions lack a rule for the post-insertion configuration visible here: the red indicator is on and the hand matches the demonstration's terminal frames. They instead say to keep closed and that the red indicator is not a release cue. To produce the recorded answer, they must explicitly require a further waypoint at [-0.0065, -0.0057, 0.0399, 3.1389, -0.0029, -1.3927] with the gripper opening on arrival, rather than declaring completion. The box-relative geometric definition of this additional endpoint and its release condition are not supplied; this substantial additional inward move and opening are not established by the demonstrated terminal frames.

The transport rule did not specify how to recover the intended elevated staging TCP accurately from the demonstration when the gripper is partly offscreen. Use the end-of-transport geometry around V176, projecting the visible held peg at its elevated height and applying the grasp-to-tip offset, rather than estimating a clearance beyond the box. Here that should give approximately [-0.0952, 0.3035, 0.1895]; my y=0.325 placed staging 2.15 cm too far outward. The phase and closed-gripper choice were already correct.

The descent rule incorrectly says to retain the elevated staging x,y. Here the low staging pose also moves inward toward the box: from the current y=0.3222 to approximately 0.3035 m, with x approximately -0.0928 and z approximately 0.0396 m. It should direct me to recover the low staging position independently from the demonstrated descent, rather than treat descent as vertical or preserve the elevated approach's nominal y. Keep the peg closed and the insertion orientation.

The terminal-pose inference needed a more explicit geometric anchor: at E205, matching V208 after the initial advance, place the TCP at the demonstrated final grasp position outside the entered box face, not at the opening or free-tip position. For this scene that endpoint is approximately [-0.1003, 0.1443, 0.0389], a remaining inward displacement of about 0.112 m rather than my 0.140 m. Preserve the current insertion yaw (about 1.5425) and keep the gripper closed. The instruction to fit final geometry did not settle the grasp-to-face offset accurately enough.

The elevated transport target must be fitted to the demonstrated end of transport near V176, rather than assumed to be directly above the low staging pose at z=0.19 m. For this cycle that target is approximately [0.0636, 0.1637, 0.1695], with the gripper closed: about 2.9 cm farther in +y and 2.1 cm lower than my answer. The instruction should distinguish this elevated transport geometry from the subsequent low staging geometry and preserve the demonstrated slight tilt (orientation approximately [3.1365, -0.1238, -1.5898]) instead of imposing a perfectly downward hand.

The descent rule incorrectly fixes staging height at 0.039–0.041 m and keeps the elevated staging x,y. At E172, the demonstrated low staging configuration requires a combined descent and horizontal correction to approximately [0.0624, 0.1452, 0.0206], keeping the peg closed in the gripper. The instruction should derive this low pose from the demonstrated pre-advance configuration and opening alignment, including the held peg's actual tilt (pitch approximately -0.1241, yaw -1.5897), rather than forcing a level hand and a 0.04 m TCP height. The elevated transport endpoint is not directly above this low staging target.

The instruction incorrectly makes completion of the initial horizontal advance a cue to go directly to the terminal demonstration pose. At E214 the green free tip is still outside the opening; the next waypoint should be another approximately 5.4 cm inward advance, to [0.0599, 0.0412, 0.0434], keeping the gripper closed and approximately preserving the current alignment, rather than jumping to y=0. It should distinguish this intermediate opening-entry configuration from the final insertion configuration and prioritize the visible tip-to-opening relationship over the assumption that one advance has already completed.

The descent rule needed a more explicit connection from the demonstrated closing frames V64–V80 to the grasp point on the yellow segment of the peg beside the box. Here that nominal point is approximately (-0.0039, -0.1113), not the reached approach TCP (-0.017, -0.1155). Refine the grasp location from the visible peg geometry and demonstrated grasp offset before descending to z=0.01 and closing; do not treat the approach endpoint as the nominal grasp location. My answer copied that endpoint despite the existing general warning against doing so.

The elevated approach localization rule needed a more precise connection from the demonstrated end-of-transport geometry around V160–V176 to the TCP staging position. At this completed pickup lift, the required approach is approximately [0.0719, -0.2692, 0.1902], with yaw 1.6773 and gripper closed. My estimate placed it 1.58 cm too far in negative y. Specify fitting the TCP position at the demonstrated transport endpoint, accounting for the grasp-to-tip offset, rather than choosing an approximate clearance outside the box face.

The instruction identified the descent correctly but did not make the box-relative staging localization precise enough. At E163 the intended low staging TCP is approximately (0.0715, -0.2693, 0.0402), not the rounded transport endpoint (0.065, -0.280, 0.040). It should specify how to fit the demonstrated staging geometry to the current box and held peg to obtain this nominal x,y before descending, rather than anchoring the descent to the reported elevated TCP. Keep the gripper closed and preserve the insertion yaw.

The descent rule needed a concrete way to recover the demonstrated grasp point on the mint end from the calibrated current wrist image and the demonstration closing frames. Here that nominal point is approximately (-0.0992, 0.0604), not the reported approach TCP (-0.1100, 0.0585). I effectively reused the approach x despite its roughly 11 mm tracking offset. Explicitly require relocalizing the demonstrated mint-end grasp point before descending to z=0.01 and closing, rather than treating the observed approach endpoint as the grasp target.

The transport-target reconstruction needed a more precise anchor: use the end of elevated transport around V176–V192, then the low staging geometry around V208 to recover the TCP's intended box-relative x,y, accounting for the offset between the visible held peg and TCP. For this cycle that elevated target is approximately [0.1180, 0.1677, 0.1885], with yaw -1.6825 and gripper closed, not [0.1000, 0.2100, 0.1900]. The instruction identified the correct transport phase but did not make that geometric reconstruction precise enough to avoid the 4.2 cm lateral and 1.8 cm longitudinal errors.

The descent rule incorrectly requires the same staging x,y as the elevated approach. Here the low staging target also moves inward along -y: from the current y=0.1809 to approximately 0.1669 m, with x approximately 0.119 m and z=0.0385 m, keeping the gripper closed. The instruction should distinguish the demonstrated low staging position from the elevated transport position and recover its horizontal offset from the demonstration rather than mandate a purely vertical descent.

The instruction did not adequately distinguish an intermediate insertion waypoint from the final demonstrated success pose. At E228, continue inward by about 0.048 m in -y, with only about -0.002 m in x, targeting TCP [0.1003, 0.069, 0.0387] and keeping the gripper closed. Do not extrapolate directly to the V245 terminal configuration at y near zero. The final frames should establish insertion alignment and destination, not imply that the entire remaining insertion must be completed in this single waypoint.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
The failures occurred while reproducing a demonstrated peg grasp and box-side insertion. The memory already retained the entire demonstration, but the policy sometimes chose the opposite end of the correct peg, reused a displaced reached TCP as the grasp or staging target, estimated transport clearance instead of reconstructing the demonstrated transport pose, or jumped from the first insertion advance directly to the final success configuration. These are SUFFICIENCY failures in the action rules, not demonstrated failures of memory retention or updating. Make the following changes in manipulation order.

For pickup, strengthen the distinction between peg identity, grasped end, and grasp position. Determine the segment actually between the fingertips using closing and early lifting frames together; the prominently visible projecting segment can be the free end, not the grasped end. Trace the grasped segment back to the unobstructed initial peg. Fit its endpoints and color boundary in the current calibrated views, then locate the demonstrated contact point along that segment. Use that nominal contact point for the open approach, closing descent, and pickup lift. At the elevated open-hand configuration, recompute that point from the visible peg rather than substituting the reported TCP. The demonstrated nominal approach and contact x,y can be identical even when the reached approach is displaced by more than a centimetre. Retain the nominal pickup heights of 0.20 m and 0.01 m and the demonstrated pickup yaw.

For transport and staging, replace the assertion that elevated transport is directly above low staging with separate reconstruction of the two poses. Identify the end of elevated transport by the demonstration's completed lateral relocation and rotation before descent; identify low staging by the configuration before the first inward advance. Fit each pose relative to the entered box face. Use the visible peg endpoints, color boundary, and fingertip geometry together to recover the TCP-to-peg offset. When the hand is partly outside the image, use the visible held peg and its demonstrated grasp offset rather than adding an arbitrary clearance beyond the face. Project elevated geometry at its elevated height, not onto the tabletop. Fit multiple neighboring demonstration frames to reduce ambiguity from occlusion, and use the current wrist image to constrain the actual held-peg offset. The TCP is neither the free tip nor the opening center.

Remove the universal constraints that transport height is approximately 0.19 m, staging height is approximately 0.04 m, pitch is zero, and descent preserves x,y. Those are common configurations, not invariants. The demonstrations also include a tilted transport at approximately 0.17 m, followed by staging near 0.021 m with pitch approximately -0.124 radians and a small inward translation during descent. Preserve such demonstrated tilt and reconstruct the TCP height needed to put the free tip at the opening. For nearly level demonstrations, the existing approximately 0.19 m transport and 0.04 m staging heights remain useful initial estimates. Compute the staging target independently of the measured transport endpoint; ordinary transport tracking error must not become a new target. Resolve the yaw's pi ambiguity from the actual held-to-free-end vector, not solely from the undirected peg axis or face normal.

For inward motion, remove the rule that completion of one approximately 0.05 m advance necessarily calls for the terminal demonstration pose. Distinguish low staging, an opening-entry configuration, and terminal insertion using the current motion frames, visible free-tip-to-opening relationship, and ordered demonstration configurations. Initial entry can include height and pitch correction: in the tilted case the TCP rises from low staging toward approximately 0.045 m while the hand becomes more nearly level. It is not always a constant-height horizontal translation.

After an advance, determine whether a demonstrated intermediate entry configuration remains before terminal insertion. If the free tip is still outside and such an intermediate configuration is evident, target that configuration rather than skipping to the final success image; the observed remaining entry advances are approximately 0.05 m. If the appropriate next configuration is terminal insertion, reconstruct the final grasp/TCP position outside the entered face, accounting for the remaining exposed peg length. Do not place the TCP at the opening or infer insertion depth from the free tip alone. The remaining distance varies substantially: it can be about 0.023 m or exceed 0.10 m. Neither a fixed second advance nor a universal 0.05 m cap is supported. Use the final frames to establish terminal geometry, but not to erase intermediate configurations visible in the demonstration. Keep the gripper closed through these demonstrated grasp, transport, staging, and insertion motions.

Narrow the completion wording: a red indicator confirms successful insertion but does not itself specify an additional waypoint or gripper command. Do not claim that the retained demonstration determines an unseen post-success continuation. The additional move-and-release behavior in the supplied record requires a separately specified action convention; its exact destination cannot be reconstructed merely by fitting the demonstration's terminal insertion pose.
proposal.refused:
No memory-field changes are justified by these reports. Every failed execution decision carried the complete, unchanged demonstration list, and no report identified an earlier execution fact that had become unavailable. Adding a phase counter, remembered waypoint, or episode-specific numeric target would not address the demonstrated cause and would require separate evidence of necessity.

Several pickup reports describe the descent as needing a different nominal x,y from the elevated approach. The recorded nominal approach and pickup targets actually share x,y; the difference is between the intended target and the physically reached TCP. Likewise, most reported staging descent corrections are transport tracking-error corrections, not evidence that every descent must move inward. Those interpretations are excluded. Independent low-staging reconstruction is retained because a genuinely tilted demonstration does have distinct elevated and low staging geometry.

The reports repeatedly supply exact world-coordinate answers for individual scenes. Those coordinates are diagnostic examples, not general action rules. They are not passed on as lookup cases or as facts to be inserted into memory. More explicit geometric fitting is warranted, but these images and reports do not establish a guaranteed centimetre-accurate reconstruction procedure for every occluded commanded target; an observed reached pose is not automatically the original command.

One report requests a substantial further inward move with opening after the red success indicator appears. The recorded action does have that behavior, so the unconditional keep-closed wording cannot cover the entire recorded continuation. However, the demonstration ends at successful insertion and supplies no geometric definition for that extra destination. A general release waypoint cannot honestly be inferred from this single continuation. The exact requested endpoint and a universal red-means-release rule are therefore not passed on; a separate post-success action specification is needed.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Preserve the demonstrated grasp location along the selected colored segment, not the peg midpoint. Recover this location from the closing and lifting demonstration frames, consulting unobstructed earlier frames. Use a downward hand, roll approximately -pi and pitch approximately zero. At pickup, align the hand's longitudinal axis with the peg and close across its width; choose the yaw equivalent that matches the demonstration.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Determine peg identity, grasped end, and contact position separately. Use closing and early lifting demonstration frames together to identify the segment actually between the fingertips; the prominently projecting segment may be the free end. Trace the grasped segment back to the unobstructed initial peg. Fit its endpoints and color boundary in the current calibrated views and recover the demonstrated contact position along that segment, rather than using the peg midpoint. At pickup use a downward hand, roll approximately -pi and pitch approximately zero, align the hand's longitudinal axis with the peg, and close across its width; choose the yaw equivalent that matches the demonstration. For later manipulation, reconstruct the demonstrated orientation rather than imposing zero pitch.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Estimate the nominal location from the peg geometry, not from the slightly displaced reported TCP after the approach.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Recompute the nominal contact location from the visible peg geometry at the elevated open-hand configuration, not from the reached TCP. Use this same nominal x,y for the open approach, closing descent, and pickup lift. A reached approach displaced by more than a centimetre does not imply that the intended approach and contact locations differ.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If the selected peg has been lifted but has not yet been transported to the insertion approach, move closed to the demonstrated elevated approach pose. This pose is directly above the low horizontal insertion staging pose, with TCP height about 0.19 m. Rotate about the vertical axis so that the free peg tip points normally into the demonstrated box face. Account for which end is held: matching the box normal alone does not determine the correct yaw, and the wrong pi-equivalent yaw reverses the tip. Determine the staging x,y from the demonstrated pre-insertion geometry, box location, peg length, and actual grasp offset. In particular, use the frames after transport and before the first horizontal advance to distinguish this pose from the pickup lift. Do not move directly from pickup into the opening.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: If the selected peg has been lifted but has not yet been transported to the insertion approach, move closed to the demonstrated elevated transport endpoint. Identify this endpoint by completed lateral relocation and rotation before descent, and reconstruct it separately from the low staging pose before inward entry. Fit each pose relative to the entered box face using neighboring demonstration frames, visible peg endpoints, color boundary, and fingertip geometry. Recover the TCP-to-peg offset and constrain the actual held-peg offset with the current wrist image. If the hand is partly outside the image, infer its position from the visible held peg and demonstrated grasp offset, not an arbitrary clearance beyond the face. Project elevated geometry at its elevated height, not onto the tabletop. The TCP is neither the free tip nor the opening center. Resolve yaw's pi ambiguity using the directed vector from the held end to the free end. Reproduce demonstrated transport tilt and height; approximately 0.19 m is only an initial estimate for nearly level transport, not a universal target. Do not assume the transport endpoint lies directly above low staging, and do not move directly from pickup into the opening.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If the hand is at the elevated insertion staging pose, descend closed to the same intended staging x,y, at TCP z approximately 0.039–0.041 m. Correct transport tracking error using the intended box-relative staging geometry rather than preserving the reported transport endpoint. The peg stays horizontal and its centerline must match the opening height. If the hand is at this low staging pose and the free tip is still outside the opening, advance approximately 0.05 m along the inward face normal, maintaining alignment and a TCP height approximately 0.037–0.039 m. Small lateral corrections should align the free tip with the opening, not the TCP with the opening.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: If the hand is at the elevated transport endpoint, move closed to the independently reconstructed low staging pose immediately before inward entry. Compute its intended box-relative position rather than preserving the measured transport endpoint. Ordinary transport tracking error is not evidence of a demonstrated inward translation during descent; include such translation only when the demonstrated geometry supports it. Reconstruct height and pitch together so the free tip approaches the opening correctly. For nearly level staging, TCP height near 0.04 m is an initial estimate, not an invariant; preserve demonstrated lower or tilted staging when present. If the hand is at low staging, target the next demonstrated opening-entry configuration. Entry may combine inward translation with height and pitch correction rather than remaining horizontal at constant height. Align the free tip with the opening, not the TCP.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If that initial horizontal advance has completed, continue inward to the demonstrated terminal insertion configuration. Infer the required endpoint from the retained demonstration's final frames and the current box and held-peg geometry. Do not use a fixed second advance: the examples include both a short remaining advance of about 0.01 m and advances exceeding 0.10 m. Peg length and the distance from the grasp to the free tip matter. Fit the visible peg and gripper geometry at the final demonstration pose to determine the desired TCP position; maintain the insertion yaw and opening height. Keep the gripper closed throughout lifting, transport, descent, and insertion. The red box indicator is evidence of success, not a cue to release the peg.

fields.name: demonstration
fields.description: At the video cycle, write all supplied V frame labels in chronological order, including the last frame. At every act cycle copy the incoming list unchanged; do not replace demonstration images with execution images. If no demonstration has yet been supplied, write an empty list. e.g. ["V0", "V16", "V32", "V48", "V64", "V80", "V96", "V112", "V128", "V144", "V160", "V176", "V192", "V208", "V222"]
fields.annotation: The ordered list of every frame label supplied in the video cycle, including the last frame. This preserves the demonstrated manipulation: which peg was selected, where along that peg it was grasped, and the approach and insertion geometry. Write the list at the video cycle and carry it unchanged through every act cycle. Before a video has been supplied the value is an empty list. e.g. ["V0", "V16", "V32", "V48", "V64", "V80", "V96", "V112", "V128", "V144", "V160", "V176", "V192", "V208", "V222"]

Track the selected peg backward to its initial position; do not select by color alone, since multiple pegs can share colors. Distinguish grasping an end from inserting that end: the free end enters the box. The selected box face can be on either image side. Robot left is +y, which appears on the right of the front image.

Use calibrated image geometry rather than copying episode-specific world coordinates. Recover tabletop peg axes and endpoints by intersecting camera rays with their appropriate height planes. Use the current motion frames to distinguish a completed lift from completed transport and a completed descent from completed horizontal insertion. Compare the current configuration to the retained demonstration when the current wrist view shows only the held peg or table; do not interpret an occluded box as a missing box. Allow approximately centimetre-scale tracking error when recognizing a completed long move, but compute the next waypoint from the intended geometry.

For an unlisted or uncertain configuration, localize the held peg, box, and closest demonstrated configuration again. If holding the peg with uncertain clearance, lift vertically to safe clearance before correcting alignment; if empty, approach the demonstrated peg open. Never insert blindly when the free tip is visibly misaligned. Use a small corrective waypoint when necessary, and never issue an identical TCP waypoint merely to change the gripper. No purposeless waiting is required.
